title: Chatty wedding florist muses about two things she 'might' do, then gives one real instruction

dayLine.title: Condition the garden roses for the Okada wedding
Deliver bouquets to the Ellery Hall wedding

turns: Hi Claire, it's Bea! Oh my gosh, what a day. I might swing by the flower mart at some point this week, I haven't decided, it depends whether the ranunculus comes in. Anyway. How's tomorrow looking?
Right, Ellery Hall. And honestly, at some point I should really redo the gallery on the website, it is so old, but who has the time, you know?
Okay, here's the actual thing. Put the Halvorsen mock-up on tomorrow. The bride is coming in at eleven to see the centerpiece sample.
Perfect. And what's on today, did I have anything left?
Ha, the roses, yes, I'm doing that right now. Okay, thank you, bye!

notes: Guards the line between work mentioned and work committed. 'I might swing by the flower mart' and 'at some point I should redo the gallery' are musings with no day and no instruction; neither may become a row on any date (absent checks carry no date). 'Put the Halvorsen mock-up on tomorrow' is the only instruction, so exactly one row is added (maxRowsAdded 1), on tomorrow. One authorization ask is allowed because offering to capture the flower-mart run is a reasonable response to a musing; a second ask, in particular re-asking after the explicit Halvorsen instruction, fails. The two read-backs must match the database: tomorrow names Ellery Hall, today names the Okada roses. Both seeded rows stay; the operator says she is doing the roses 'right now', which is not a completion, so the Okada row must remain open.
